name: SE_StringNextCharPos
semantics: UTF-8 aware 'next character start'. s = string of arg1 (CellGetString: cell tag 2 = pool string, tag 0xb = heap string; any other tag -> NULL). If s is NULL returns 0. pos = raw dword of arg2, compared UNSIGNED with strlen(s). If pos >= len (so any negative pos too) returns len. Else returns the smallest index j > pos with s[j]==0 or (s[j]&0xC0)!=0x80, i.e. the byte offset of the character that follows the one containing byte pos (scan starts at s[pos+1]). Result is always in (pos, len].
notes: Handler 0x4ac3b5 (case 9). Counterpart of SE_StringPrevCharPos. Termination guaranteed by the NUL.

name: SE_GetSuperClass
semantics: Parent class id of an object's class. If arg1 cell tag==0xA (object ref): obj = cell value; if obj+8 (class pointer) is 0 (dead/invalid object) -> return 0. Any other tag: ctx = Script::ResolveObjectContext(raw dword of the cell): value >= 0 -> static class-table lookup by CLASS ID (FindClassRecord), value < 0 -> script-created object hash lookup by -value-1; ctx==0 -> return 0. Then class = ctx[+8]; parent = class[+0x10]; returns 0 if parent == -1 (no parent), else parent (a class id as int). So it works for a plain int class id as well as for object refs.
notes: Handler 0x4ad8fc (case 0x3b). The class record field read is +0x10 (parent CLASS ID, -1 = none); SE_GetClass (0x39) returns class[+0]. script_vm.md lists the parent at +0x14, the code reads +0x10. A tag-0xA cell holding a NULL pointer would fault (the pointer itself is not checked).

name: SE_GetDir
semantics: Directory listing. dir = arg1 string; pattern = arg2 string if argc>=2 (non-string -> default) else "*.*"; userDir = (arg3 raw dword != 0) if argc>=3 else 0. Builds '<normalized dir>\<pattern>' (NormalizeGamePath: '/' -> '\'; with userDir=1 the dir is first prefixed with the Egosoft user directory, otherwise it is relative to the game's current directory) and enumerates with _findfirst64i32/_findnext64i32. Counts ALL returned entries (files AND sub-directories, including '.' and '..' when the pattern matches them), then re-enumerates and returns a NEW array of that many strings holding the bare entry names in file-system enumeration order. If _findfirst fails or there are 0 entries returns int 0 (not an empty array).
notes: Handler 0x4ade56 (case 0x73). Two passes (count, then fill) so a directory changing in between gives stale or short names. File::FindFirstWrapper 0x004d2950, Archive::FindNextFile 0x004e9560. Reads the real file system.

name: SE_StringNumChars
semantics: Number of characters of s (not bytes) with the game's text convention: scan bytes; a byte with (b&0xC0)==0x80 (UTF-8 continuation) is not counted; a byte 0x1B (ESC) is not counted AND the byte after it is skipped too (colour/format escape pair); every other byte counts 1. Non-string arg1 (CellGetString NULL) -> 0. Empty string -> 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ac367. If the string ends in a lone 0x1B the scan steps past the terminating NUL (reads beyond the string; undefined). Only arg1 is read.

name: SE_XMLImportValue
semantics: Inverse of SE_XMLExportValue. Parses arg1 (XML text) with libxml (LoadPckXml). Parse failure -> int 0. Root = first node of type element (xmlDocGetRootElement + sibling walk); none -> int 0. Otherwise Script::XmlToValue(root) builds a cell which is returned (ownership moved): the node must be an element named 'sval' (case-insens.), otherwise an EMPTY cell (tag 0) is returned. Attribute type selects: 'int' -> int cell from attr val (default 0); 'string' -> string cell from attr val; 'float' -> double cell (tag 0xE) from the val attribute; 'array' -> attr size=N (N<1 -> empty array of size 0), then every element child (the 'sval' name test inside the loop is applied to the PARENT node, so all element children are imported; a child that is not an sval gives an empty cell) is imported recursively and stored at index 0,1,2..; 'table' -> new table, attr size, element children alternate key, value, key, value... (TableInsertAndGrow); any other or missing type -> empty cell (tag 0). The libxml doc is freed.
notes: Handler 0x4ae7ce (case 0x68) -> Script::XmlToValue 0x004a7c90. A non-string arg1 passes NULL into the xml read (no type check) -> crash. Types match ValueToXml: int, string, float, array, table.

name: SE_TaskExists
semantics: Returns 1 if a task with id = raw dword of arg1 exists in the VM task table (vm[0], hash map keyed by task id: bucket = id & (nBuckets-1), node key at +4, task pointer at +8), else 0. The calling task itself exists. Arg type is not checked. Implemented with the generic id->pointer lookup that Ghidra names Cockpit::FindByHandle.
notes: Handler 0x4abfa9 (case 0x35). Result normalised to 0/1 (NEG/SBB/NEG). Task ids come from SE_GetTaskID / task start natives; ids of finished tasks disappear from the map.

name: SE_TableClear
semantics: In-place clear. If arg1 cell tag is 9 (table) and the table object pointer is non-NULL: destroys key and value cells of every node (releasing refcounts of contained arrays/tables/strings), frees all nodes and the bucket array, then resets the header: buckets=NULL (+8), auto-key counter (+0x10)=1, bucket count (+0xc)=4, entry count (+0x14)=0. The table object and all references to it stay valid and are now empty. Any other arg type: silent no-op. Always returns int 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ad806 (case 0x33) -> Script::TableClear 0x004a83e0. The counter at +0x10 is the 'next numbered key' used by TableAppendNextKey, so numbering restarts at 1 after a clear.

name: SE_StringPrevCharPos
semantics: UTF-8 aware 'previous character start'. s NULL (non-string arg1) -> 0. Util::Utf8PrevCharOffset(s, pos): pos is taken UNSIGNED; if pos==0 return 0; len=strlen(s); if pos>len then pos=len (a negative pos therefore becomes len); i=pos; loop { i-=1; if i==0 return 0; if (s[i]&0xC0)!=0x80 return i; }. So it returns the start offset of the character that precedes byte position pos; for pos=1 (or when only continuation bytes precede) it returns 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ac41c (case 0xa), helper Util::Utf8PrevCharOffset 0x004ee6a0 (EDI=s, EDX=pos).

name: SE_GetLanguage
semantics: Returns the current game language id: the dword at Init::g_pEngineConfig(0x00606f34)+0x76c (same numbers as the language ids of the text files, e.g. 44 English, 49 German, 33 French, 7 Russian). Pure read, no args.
notes: Handler 0x4ac1d9 (case 5). The same field selects the per-language text slot vm+0x334+lang*4 used by SE_ReadText / SE_ExistsText.

name: SE_SetProfiling
semantics: No-op in the release build: arguments ignored, returns int 0 immediately (the handler is the same stub that SE_SignData uses).
notes: Handler 0x004abea2 (case 0x7b) is literally ResumeTaskWithIntVm(task, vm, 0). The script-side flag Cheats.profilingActive is separate.

name: SE_MakeDir
semantics: Creates ONE directory (Win32 CreateDirectoryA, not recursive) at path RELATIVE TO THE EGOSOFT USER DIRECTORY (File::MakeDirectory is always called with inUserDir=1: the path becomes '<EgosoftUserDir>\<path>' with '/' converted to '\'). Returns 1 if the directory was created, 0 on any failure (already exists, parent missing, invalid path). File-system side effect. Non-string arg1 -> NULL path.
notes: Handler 0x4adf67 (case 0x74). The comment on File::MakeDirectory 0x004d2a60 says 'or already existed' but CreateDirectoryError returns -1 for ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, so an existing directory gives 0.

name: SE_LogFunc
semantics: Logarithmic interpolation. 5 args read as raw dwords (no type/argc check): x=a1, lo=a2, hi=a3, outLo=a4, outHi=a5. x is clamped to [lo,hi] (if x<lo x=lo; then if x>hi x=hi; signed). Result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) * ln(x/lo) / ln(hi/lo) ) in x87 extended precision (FYL2X*ln2); (outHi-outLo) is an int32 subtraction (wraps). Ftol truncates toward zero (double -> CVTTSD2SI); NaN/inf/overflow (lo=0, lo<0, lo==hi giving 0/0 ...) give 0x80000000 (-2147483648). x<=lo -> outLo, x>=hi -> outHi.
notes: Handler 0x4ace0e -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntLog 0x004a5e70 (EDX=outHi). Python doubles can differ from x87 80-bit only at exact integer boundaries.

name: SE_KGV
semantics: Least common multiple (German KGV) = (a / gcd) * b with 32-bit wrap (signed IDIV/IMUL, low 32 bits), where gcd comes from SUBTRACTIVE Euclid: while a!=b { if a>b a-=b else b-=a }. a==b returns b. ZERO or NEGATIVE inputs never terminate (e.g. a=0,b=5: b-=0 forever; a<0 makes b grow) -> the game hangs inside the native (no scheduler yield). Large coprime values are slow (O(max) iterations).
notes: Handler 0x4acf54 (case 0x45). SE_GGT (0x44) is the same loop returning the gcd. Emulator should treat a<=0 or b<=0 as an infinite loop error.

name: SE_IsPosInRangeA
semantics: Is the point arg1=[x,y,z] inside any sphere of arg2? arg2 is a flat array of pairs: element 2i = array[3] {cx,cy,cz} (int cells), element 2i+1 = radius (int). If arg1 is not an array with 3 elements -> 0. maxPairs = arg3 raw dword if argc>2 else -1 (all). n = array size of arg2 (abs of the stored size, 0 if not an array); if maxPairs>=0 and 2*maxPairs < n then n = 2*maxPairs. Loop i=0,2,4.. while i<n: element i must be an array (tag 8) with 3 usable sub-elements, else the pair is skipped; dist = Ftol(sqrt((x-cx)^2+(y-cy)^2+(z-cz)^2)) (int32 differences, converted by FILD, squares and sum in x87 extended precision, the sum rounded to float32 before FSQRT, Ftol truncates); hit if dist <= radius (signed int compare, radius = raw dword of element i+1). Returns 1 on the first hit, 0 if none.
notes: Handler 0x4ad11d (case 0x49) -> Script::PointInAnySphere 0x004af930 (ECX=maxPairs). Radius element i+1 is dereferenced without a NULL check: an odd-length array whose last element is a valid centre array crashes. The compare uses the TRUNCATED distance (a point at distance radius+0.9 counts as inside).

name: SE_ExpFunc
semantics: Exponential interpolation, args as SE_LogFunc: x=a1, lo=a2, hi=a3, outLo=a4, outHi=a5. x clamped to [lo,hi]. Result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) * exp(x/lo) / exp(hi/lo) ) (x87 f2xm1/fscale, extended precision). The exponents are x/lo and hi/lo (NOT (x-lo)/...): at x==hi the result is outHi exactly, at x==lo it is outLo+d*exp(1)/exp(hi/lo), not outLo. Ftol truncates toward zero; lo==0 or overflow -> 0x80000000.
notes: Handler 0x4ace3b -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntExp 0x004a5ed0. No arg checks.

name: SE_DistanceA3
semantics: Euclidean distance between the point in array arg1 and the point (a2,a3,a4). Elements 0,1,2 of arg1 are fetched with ArrayGetElement (lazy arrays are materialised with int 0); if arg1 is not an array or has fewer than 3 elements -> returns int 0. Element values and a2..a4 are raw dwords (no type check). dx=A[0]-a2, dy=A[1]-a3, dz=A[2]-a4 (int32 wrapping subtraction), each converted to float32 (FSTP float: rounded to a 24-bit mantissa for |d|>2^24); the squares and sum are evaluated in x87 extended precision, the sum goes into FSQRT as a float; result = Ftol(sqrt(...)) truncated toward zero (floor for non-negative).
notes: Handler 0x4acfbf (case 0x47) -> Math::VecLengthToInt 0x0049c880 -> Math::SqrtF (FLD float; FSQRT). SE_Distance3 (0x46) is the same with 3 plain int args.

name: SE_DeleteFile
semantics: Deletes a file via File::Delete(path, flag): flag = (arg2 raw dword != 0) if argc>=2 else 0; flag=1 means path relative to the Egosoft user directory, 0 relative to the game directory (NormalizeGamePath, '/' -> '\'); uses CRT remove(). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (file missing, no permission). Real file-system side effect. Non-string path -> NULL into NormalizeGamePath (undefined / crash).
notes: Handler 0x4add5c (case 0x6f). File::Delete 0x004e96c0 returns 1 when Crt::Remove()==0.

name: SE_XMLImportText
semantics: Parses arg1 as XML TEXT (the document contents, not a file name) with libxml (Script::LoadPckXml -> xmlReadMemory). Parse failure (NULL doc) -> 0. Takes the root element (xmlDocGetRootElement) and walks it and its siblings for the first ELEMENT named 'language' (case-insensitive); in practice the root element itself must be <language id="N">; none found -> 0. Script::ParseLanguageElement: attribute id (atol); if id>0, for every child element named 'page' (case-insens.) ParsePageXml(vm, id, page): page id attr (atol) is mapped (380000..399999 -> id-380000, 350000..379999 -> id-350000, 300001..349999 -> id-300000, otherwise unchanged); every child <t id="K">text</t> (element name 't', case-insens.) is stored with text = node content passed through UnescapeTextPageString (rules: see SE_ConvertTextString) and its stored length, into the language slot vm+0x334+id*4 (StoreTextPageEntries; existing ids of that page are replaced/added). Returns 1 when a language element was found and parsed, else 0. The libxml doc is freed afterwards.
notes: Handler 0x4ae659 (case 0). A non-string arg1 leaves a NULL pointer that is passed straight to strlen/xmlReadMemory (no type check) -> access violation. Used to load language files as strings.

name: SE_XMLExportValue
semantics: Serialises ANY value cell to XML text. Script::ValueToXml builds an <sval> element tree, puts it as root into a new document (version '1.0') and dumps it with xmlDocDumpFormatMemory(format=1): the text starts with '<?xml version="1.0"?>' and a newline, then the indented element tree, newline terminated. Encoding: int (tag 1): <sval type="int" val="N"/>; strings (tags 2, 0xB): <sval type="string" val="text"/> (XML-escaped by libxml); double (tag 0xE): type="float" with val written by XmlSetValDouble; array (tag 8): type="array" size="N" with one child sval per element in order; table (tag 9): type="table" size="entry count" with children key1,value1,key2,value2,... in table iteration order (TableNextEntry = bucket order, not insertion order); every other tag (empty 0, object ref 0xA, function 3, ...): type="unknown" typeid="<tag byte>" (the value itself is lost). Returns the text as a new string; returns int 0 only if node allocation fails.
notes: Handler 0x4ae750 (case 0x67). The attribute-name strings 'int' etc. were taken from XmlToValue's comparisons; the exact val formatting of floats (XmlSetValDouble) was not examined.

name: SE_VerifyData
semantics: Signature check through Windows CryptoAPI (provider 'Microsoft Base Cryptographic Provider v1.0', container 'X2EgosoftCSPContainer'). Needs argc==3 EXACTLY, arg1 a string with length>0, arg2 a string with length>0, arg3 an array (tag 8) with size>0; any violation returns int 0. The key blob = the low byte of every element of arg3 (n bytes). Script::VerifySignature: CryptImportKey(blob), MD5 (CALG_MD5 0x8003) of the strlen(arg1) bytes of arg1, base64-decode of arg2 (length must be a multiple of 4), CryptVerifySignatureA. SUCCESS: returns the base64 text of the MD5 digest (24 chars) as a string; any failure (bad key, bad signature, no provider) returns int 0. So the script gets either the digest string or 0. Otherwise pure computation (a CSP key container is created as a side effect).
notes: Handler 0x4af3b2 (case 0x95). The game does not refuse a script on failure (x3-mod doc script-signature-check.md). An emulator without the real key can return 0, or - to model 'signature valid' - base64(MD5(arg1)).

name: SE_Time
semantics: Current wall-clock time: __time64(NULL) truncated to a signed 32-bit int = seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. No args. Emulator may return int(time.time()).
notes: Handler 0x4ae48c (case 0x89). SE_CTime (24, not in list) uses the same call but takes an optional time argument.

name: SE_TableFind
semantics: Lookup. Script::TableFindValue(key=arg2 cell, table=arg1 cell): if arg1 is not a table (tag 9), has no buckets, or the key is absent -> returns int 0 (indistinguishable from a stored 0; SE_TableExists tells presence). Keys: only int (tag 1, matched by tag+value) and string (tags 2 and 0xB, matched by case-SENSITIVE byte content; pool and heap strings compare equal); any other key type finds nothing. On a hit the VALUE cell is copied into the result (CopyCell: arrays/tables/strings/objects shared by reference with refcount+1, doubles deep-copied) and returned.
notes: Handler 0x4ad539 (case 0x2a). Hash: int key = v & (n-1); string h = c + 2h.

name: SE_SmoothInterpolate
semantics: Logistic S-curve mapping; args a1..a5 = inLo, inHi, outLo, outHi, x (x is the LAST arg here). t = (x-inLo)/(inHi-inLo) (floating, not clamped; inHi==inLo -> inf/NaN); result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) / (1 + exp(-15*(t-0.5))) ) with the constants 0.5 and -15.0 stored as float32; x87 extended precision; Ftol truncates toward zero; NaN -> 0x80000000. Not normalised: at t=0 it gives outLo+d*0.00055, at t=1 outLo+d*0.99945 (never exactly the end values); outside [inLo,inHi] it keeps flattening, no clamp.
notes: Handler 0x4ace68 -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntSigmoid 0x004a5f50. (The clamped linear SE_LinFunc 0x3e takes x0,x1,y0,y1,x.)

name: SE_SignGameStats
semantics: Signs a string with the game's built-in private key (MD5 + CryptSignHashA via Script::SignDataBase64) and returns the base64 signature. Needs argc==1 and arg1 a string with length>0, else int 0. Returns the EMPTY STRING (not 0) when: the story-data copy pointer vm+0x145c is NULL, or bit 0x10 of vm+0x12f0 is set (signing disabled), or Script::VerifyStoryFiles(vm+0x145c, vm+0x1460) fails (the loaded x3story data differs from the stock signature, i.e. modified scripts cannot sign). If SignDataBase64 itself fails (returns NULL) the result is int 0. Otherwise the base64 signature string. Side effect: CryptoAPI container creation.
notes: Handler 0x4af4fe (case 0x97). Used for high-score / statistics signing. 0 = bad arguments or crypto failure, '' = refused by the integrity check. An emulator running modified scripts should return '' (refusal).

name: SE_ScriptComputeExpression
semantics: Evaluates a postfix (reverse Polish) expression IN PLACE in a script array; the native itself always returns int 0, the answer is left in buf[0] (type) and buf[1] (value). LAYOUT: buf is a flat array of 2*n cells; the array data pointer is read raw, so arg1 must be a materialised tag-8 array with >= 2n cells (no bounds/type checks). Pair k = (buf[2k], buf[2k+1]) = (T, V). arg2 = n = raw dword of arg2 = PAIR count, not cell count; n<=0 -> result (0,0). OPERAND pair: T != 15; T is the type code, taken from the dword value of cell buf[2k] (its cell tag is ignored); V is any value cell (int, double, string, object ref ...). OPERATOR pair: T == 15 (0xF) and the operator code is the dword value of buf[2k+1]. TYPE CODES used by the evaluator: 0 = none/false; 4 = number (int; value cell tag 1, or tag 0xE double); 5 = string (value cell tag 2 or 0xB); any code with bit 0x10000 set (e.g. 0x10006 ship, 0x10007 station, 0x10008 sector) = object (truthiness via CellIsValidObject); anything else (e.g. 10 race) is opaque. VARIABLES AND CONSTANTS ARE NOT LOOKED UP BY THIS NATIVE: the MSCI interpreter (x3story __runScript, command 104) has already resolved every operand to a (type,value) pair (local variable -> varTypes/varValues, 1 -> this-object, others via ScriptGetConst) and filled the buffer; the native only sees resolved values. EVALUATION: a static value stack of 100 cells (50 entries of two cells: type cell, value cell) at 0x00609440, with no overflow check. For each pair in order: operand -> push an entry (type cell := int cell with value T, value cell := CopyCell(V)); operator -> as follows. BINARY operators (code < 0x10000): if the stack is empty the operator is ignored; otherwise it pops B (top) and A (second; with a single entry on the stack A is stale memory below the stack) and writes the result into A's slot; typeA/typeB are the T codes. 0 '==', 1 '!=', 2 '>', 3 '<', 4 '>=', 5 '<=': if typeA==typeB: type 4 -> cmp = A.int - B.int (32-bit wrap); type 5 -> byte-wise unsigned strcmp (case-sensitive, sign only) if both value cells really are strings (tag 2/0xB), else cmp=1; any other equal type -> cmp = A.int - B.int only if both value cells have tag 1, else cmp=1, and for these other types ONLY == and != are supported (ordering ops give false). result = cmp==0 / !=0 / >0 / <0 / >=0 / <=0. If typeA != typeB: '==' gives false, '!=' gives true, ordering ops give false. 6 '&', 7 '|', 8 '^': need typeA==4 and typeB==4 else false; if both value cells have int tag 1 then A.val = A.val op B.val, otherwise A is left unchanged (type 4). 9 '&&': an operand is falsy if its type code is 0, type 4 with value 0, or an object type that is not a valid object; every other operand (nonzero int, string, valid object, opaque type) is truthy; result true iff both truthy. 10 '||': same truth rules, true iff either truthy. 0xB '+': both type 4 -> CellAdd in place (int add wraps, int+double promotes to double); otherwise the script method static __scriptOpAddString(typeA, valueA, typeB, valueB) is called synchronously (class id 0x2be, CallMethodStatic with the task id) and if it returns a string (tag 2/0xB) the result is (type 5, that string) else false (0,0). 0xC '-', 0xD '*': need both type 4 else false; CellSubtract / CellMultiply in place. 0xE '/', 0xF '%': need both type 4 and B's value dword != 0 else false; CellDivide / CellModulo in place (int division truncates toward zero). Any other code 0x10..0xFFFF -> false. BOOLEAN RESULTS: true = (type 4, int 1); false = (type 0, int 0) -- note false carries type code 0, not 4, so a following op sees typeA=0 (e.g. (a==b)+1 goes to __scriptOpAddString). UNARY operators (code has bit 0x10000; no pop, acts on the top entry, no empty-stack check): 0x10012 bitwise NOT: type 4 -> ~value if the value cell has tag 1 (else unchanged), other types -> (0,0). 0x10013 negate: type 4 -> CellNegate (int -v, double sign flip, object ref cell converted to its int id), other types -> (0,0). 0x10014 logical NOT: type 0 -> (4,1); type 4 with value 0 -> (4,1); an object type that is not a valid object -> (4,1); everything else (nonzero int, string, valid object, other types) -> (0,0). Any other unary code -> (0,0). RESULT: if the stack holds exactly one entry at the end, its type cell and value cell are CopyCell'ed into buf[0] and buf[1] (buf[0] becomes an int cell whose value is the result TYPE code: 4 number, 5 string, 0 false/none, 0x1000x object; buf[1] holds the result value cell: int, double, string or object ref); with 0 or >1 entries buf[0] = buf[1] = int 0. Cells after buf[1] keep their old contents. The two stack base cells are cleared; native return value int 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ab8ca (case 0x5d) -> Script::EvalExpression 0x004afe60 (args: vm, task, arg1 cell, arg2 cell). x3story caller: gExprTokenBuffer with instruction[2] pairs, result read from buffer[0], buffer[1] (type, value). Quirks: (1) ordering compare uses A-B in int32 so operands differing by >2^31 misorder; (2) string compares require real string cells; (3) no stack bounds checks (max 50 entries); (4) number type 4 with double cells goes through CellAdd/Subtract/... generic arithmetic; (5) logical NOT of a nonzero int yields type-0 false, of 0 yields (4,1). Decompile checked against the disassembly of the operand/operator dispatch.

name: SE_RotateVector
semantics: Rotates the integer vector in array arg1 IN PLACE and returns int 0. Reads vec[0..2] (ArrayGetElement raw dwords; missing elements -> NULL deref crash), angA=arg2, angB=arg3 (raw dwords; 16-bit binary angles: value&0xFFFF, 65536 = full turn). Builds M with Math::AnglesToMatrix(a=angA, b=angB, c=0), 16.16 fixed point: with ca=cos(2*pi*a/65536) etc., M = Rc(c)*Rb(b)*Ra(a), Ra=[[ca,0,sa],[0,1,0],[-sa,0,ca]], Rb=[[1,0,0],[0,cb,-sb],[0,sb,cb]], Rc=[[cc,sc,0],[-sc,cc,0],[0,0,1]] (row-vector convention); with c=0 that is M=[[ca,0,sa],[sa*sb,cb,-ca*sb],[-sa*cb,sb,ca*cb]]; each entry = Ftol(value*65536) (x87, truncation toward zero; sin/cos intermediates are spilled as float32 so +-1 LSB vs exact math). Then out = v x M: out[j] = sum_i R(v[i]*M[i][j]) where R(p) = (int32)(((int64)p + 0x8000) >> 16) per product (rounded 16.16 multiply) and the three terms are summed with 32-bit wrap. out[0..2] are written back with ArraySetInt (cells replaced by int cells). Plain ints work (result = v*M/65536 rounded).
notes: Handler 0x4aeeec is shared by cmd 0x5b (this one, Math::VecMulMatrix 0x004f0da0) and cmd 0x5c SE_RotateVectorInv (Math::VecByMatrixRows 0x004f0c00: out[i]=sum_j M[i][j]*v[j], the transposed = inverse rotation). The matrix formula was recovered by running the x87 listing of Math::AnglesToMatrix 0x004f0270 numerically and fitting; truncation order matters for bit-exact results.

name: SE_RegSub
semantics: Expands a replacement template with the capture groups of the LAST SE_RegExec made with the same compiled regex. regexId = raw dword of arg1 = id returned by SE_RegComp (hash map vm+0x15f4). Unknown id -> returns the empty string. template = arg2 string (non-string -> NULL -> crash in CalcRegexReplaceLength). Henry Spencer regsub rules (Regex::Substitute): '&' = whole match (group 0); '\N' (backslash + digit 0-9) = capture group N; '\\' -> '\'; '\&' -> '&'; a backslash followed by any other char is output as a literal backslash and the next char is processed normally; all other chars are copied. An unset group (start or end pointer NULL) expands to nothing. The result goes into a buffer sized by CalcRegexReplaceLength (an upper bound) and is returned as a NEW heap string (tag 0xB). RegSub does no matching itself: if the regex never matched or the last match failed, all groups are NULL and the template is output with the group references removed. The group pointers (start at regexp+0, end at +0x28, 10 groups) point INTO the subject string passed to the last RegExec: if that string was freed or modified since, RegSub reads freed memory.
notes: Handler 0x4acbe9 (case 0x60). Regex::Substitute 0x004e6980, Script::CalcRegexReplaceLength 0x004a68b0. SE_RegSubGlobal (0x61) loops Exec/Substitute over the subject. Regex library = Henry Spencer (magic 0x9c at regexp+0x60); a faithful emulator needs a Spencer-compatible engine.

name: SE_MatrixMultiplySelfRight
semantics: In-place 3x3 matrix product: m1 := m2 x m1 (arg2 is the LEFT factor, arg1 the right factor and the destination). Each matrix is an array of 3 row arrays of 3 int cells (16.16 fixed point), read as raw dwords (missing rows/elements -> NULL deref crash). Math::MatMul: result[i][j] = sum_k R(m2[i][k]*m1[k][j]) with R(p) = (int32)(((int64)p + 0x8000) >> 16) applied per product (rounded) and the three rounded terms summed with 32-bit wrap. The 9 results are written back into the existing row arrays of arg1 via ArraySetInt (cells become int cells). arg2 is unchanged. Returns int 0.
notes: Handler 0x4aea21 (case 0x57). Case 0x58 SE_MatrixMultiplySelfLeft is m1 := m1 x m2 (0x4aeb42). Internal buffers use a row stride of 4 ints (4th unused).

name: SE_LinFuncSum
args: x0:int, x1:int, y0:int, y1:int, xa:int, xb:int
semantics: Trapezoid sum of the clamped linear ramp over an integer range. Ramp(x) = Math::ClampedLinearRamp with line (x0,y0)-(x1,y1): if x0==x1 -> (y0+y1)/2 (truncating toward zero); elif x<=x0 -> y0; elif x>=x1 -> y1; else mid=(y0+y1)/2 (trunc toward zero) plus: if x<0x10000 and (x1-x0)<0x10000: MulDiv(y1-y0, 2x-x0-x1, 2(x1-x0)) else (int32)(((int64)(y1-y0) * (x - (x0+x1)/2)) / (x1-x0)) ((x0+x1)/2 truncates toward zero; 64/32 IDIV, overflow traps). MulDiv(a,b,c) = 0 if c==0 else (int32)((int64)a*b/c) truncated toward zero. Result = ((Ramp(xa) + Ramp(xb)) * (xb - xa + 1)) / 2 with 32-bit wrap and the final /2 truncating toward zero. Args a1..a6 = x0,x1,y0,y1,xa,xb; no ordering check (xb<xa gives zero/negative counts).
notes: Handler 0x4acec4 -> Script::NativeClampedRampSum 0x004a5fb0 + Math::ClampedLinearRamp 0x0042fb20. Arg mapping verified in the disassembly: ramp calls use x0=a1, x1=a2, y0=a3, y1=a4; first x=a5, second x=a6. All ints, no type checks.

name: SE_GetAnglesFromRotMatrix
semantics: Inverse of SE_GetRotMatrixFromAngles(a,b,c) (M = Rc(c)Rb(b)Ra(a), 16.16, see SE_RotateVector). Reads the 3x3 matrix (3 row arrays of 3 ints, raw dwords; missing -> crash), calls Math::MatrixToEuler and returns a NEW array of 3 int cells [a, b, c], binary angles 0..0xFFFF (65536 = full turn). Table based (g_AsinTable with 65537 u16 entries indexed by the 16.16 value, cosine table, Math::AtanAngle), so results are table values; floats give +-1..2. With s=m[2][1] (=sin b) and cb=cos b: b = asin(s) (s>=0: table[s] in 0..0x4000; s<0: 0x10000-table[-s], i.e. 0xC000..0xFFFF); a = AtanAngle(FixedDivide(m[2][2],cb), -FixedDivide(m[2][0],cb)) (= atan2(-m20, m22)); c = AtanAngle(m[1][1]*65536/cb, m[0][1]*65536/cb) (= atan2(m01, m11)); if |s| > 0xE666 (near gimbal) a different, better conditioned formula for a is used. Gimbal s==+0x10000: b=0x4000, c=0, a=ftol(fpatan(m[0][2], m[0][0])) (minus 0x10000 if above 0xFFFF); s==-0x10000: b=-0x4000 (a NEGATIVE value), c=0, a=AtanAngle(m[0][0], m[0][2]).
notes: Handler 0x4ae8d4 (case 0x55) -> Math::MatrixToEuler 0x004f0640 (Ghidra's x87 parts unreliable; gimbal formulas uncertain). Matrix int index = row*4+col. Output array order = MatrixToEuler outputs (s04, eax, s08) = (a, b, c). An emulator without the tables can use atan2/asin in floats and round to the nearest binary angle; expect occasional off-by-one.

name: SE_FreeText
semantics: Frees ALL loaded script text pages of ALL languages: Script::FreeAllTextPages(vm) walks the 999 per-language slots vm+0x334.., removes every page entry, destroys string cells, frees the memory and zeroes the slot. Afterwards SE_ReadText / SE_ExistsText find nothing until texts are loaded again (SE_XMLImportText, SE_LoadText, SE_LoadAllTexts). Always returns int 0. Side effect on engine/VM text tables.
notes: Handler 0x4ae6a4 (case 6). Emulator: clear the text database, return 0.

name: SE_CubicPoly
args: a1:int, a2:int, a3:int, a4:int, a5:int, a6:int, x:int
semantics: Odd cubic around a centre; 7 int args a1..a7 (a7 = x). t = min(max(x - a1, -a1), a1) (first the lower clamp against -a1, then the upper against a1); r = a6/a5 (floating); c = (a4 - r*a3) / a3^3 (floating); result = Ftol( a2 + r*t + c*t^3 ) in x87 extended precision (truncation toward zero). a5==0 or a3==0 -> inf/NaN -> 0x80000000. No type/argc checks. The curve passes through a2 at t=0 with slope r and equals a2+a4 at t=a3 (as written: a2 + r*a3 + c*a3^3 = a2 + a4).
notes: Handler 0x4acef4 -> Script::NativeCubicPoly 0x004a6010 (x in ECX, a1..a6 on the stack). Formula derived instruction by instruction (FDIVRP, FCOM clamp pair); note x and the clamp centre share a1.

name: SE_ConvertTextString
semantics: Converts a text-page style string: duplicates arg1 (a non-string gives NULL; the following strlen(NULL) then crashes) and runs Script::UnescapeTextPageString IN PLACE on the copy; returns the copy as a new string. Rules (left to right over strlen bytes, with a 'skip' flag): '\n'->0x0A, '\b'->0x08, '\t'->0x09, '\r'->0x0D; '\' followed by octal digits 0-7 (any count, accumulated in 8 bits, stops at the first char outside '0'..'7') -> that byte; '\' followed by any other char -> that char literally (so '\(' gives '(' and '\\' gives '\'); a raw LF (0x0A) -> space; an unescaped '(' starts skip mode and an unescaped ')' ends it: everything (also escapes) inside is dropped and the parentheses themselves are not output; all other chars copied. QUIRK checked away (a terminator bug once assumed here was refuted 2026-10-29): the function writes no NUL terminator, but it returns the new length in EAX and the handler passes it on: ResumeTaskWithString 0x004a4860 pushes EAX as maxLen and ECX as the text for SetCellStringDup, which copies min(maxLen, strlen) bytes (Util::StrNDupReplace) and terminates. So the result is exactly the output bytes, cut at the first NUL byte (octal 000 or a lone trailing backslash give an early NUL); no tail of the input. Example: input of the 4 chars a, backslash, '(', b gives a, '(', b. Strings without backslash, parentheses or LF come out unchanged.
notes: Handler 0x4acb1a (case 0x93), Script::UnescapeTextPageString 0x004a4a60 (no store of 0 at the end; the length in EAX survives to ResumeTaskWithString at 0x004acb4f, whose register names in the database were swapped, which is how the tail was once assumed). The same function is used by text-page loading (ParsePageXml) with the stored length.

name: SE_CompressRangeData
semantics: In-place removal of spheres contained in other spheres from the flat pair array arg1 (element 2i = array[3] centre {x,y,z}, element 2i+1 = radius). maxPairs = arg2 raw dword if argc>1 else -1. n = min(arraySize/2, maxPairs) (maxPairs<0 or too large -> arraySize/2). If n<2 returns n and leaves the array untouched. Otherwise copies the n pairs into a temp table (radius,x,y,z); an element 2i that is not an array tag 8 or lacks three elements makes the native return 0 with the array untouched. Then for i=0..n-2: if r[i]>0, for j=i+1..n-1 with r[j]>0: d = Ftol(sqrt(float-cast squared centre differences)); if r[i]+d <= r[j] then r[i]=0 and break (sphere i lies inside j); else if r[j]+d <= r[i] then r[j]=0. The surviving pairs (temp radius > 0, so spheres with radius <= 0 are dropped as well) are compacted to the front of the script array in original order by copying the centre-array cell and radius cell (ArraySetElement). The array SIZE IS NOT REDUCED: slots after the compacted part keep their old values. Returns the number of surviving pairs.
notes: Handler 0x4ad1c8 (case 0x4b) -> Script::ArrayMergeContainedSpheres 0x004afbb0. Distance handling as SE_IsPosInRangeA. The radius cell at 2i+1 is read without a NULL check (crash if the length is odd).

name: SE_CallStackDump
semantics: Debug stub with no visible effect; always returns int 0. argc==0: Script::ScanTaskStack(current task) (a pure scan loop, no output). argc>0: if the arg1 cell tag==1 the task with that id is looked up (task table) and its stack scanned; other arg tags are ignored.
notes: Handler 0x4ae3f2 (case 0x80). CAUTION: a tag-1 arg with a non-existent task id makes the lookup return NULL and ScanTaskStack(NULL) dereferences it -> crash. ScanTaskStack only reads (printing was compiled out).
